name: Missouri
headline_status: Recreational and medical cannabis are legal for adults 21+.
summary: Missouri voters approved medical cannabis in 2018 and adult-use legalization through constitutional Amendment 3 in November 2022, with licensed adult-use sales starting in February 2023. Adults can possess up to three ounces and may grow at home with a state registration. A 2026 initiative to fold marijuana and hemp under alcohol-style regulation did not make the ballot, and regulators proposed new rule changes in November 2026.

adult_use_since.value: Legalized by Amendment 3, approved by voters November 8, 2022 (53.1%).

home_grow.value: Allowed with a state cultivation registration: up to 6 flowering plants, 6 non-flowering plants and 6 clones per registrant, and no more than 12 flowering plants per residence.

public_use.value: Consumption in public places is prohibited except at approved venues; a first offense carries a civil fine of up to $100.

retail_sales.value: Licensed adult-use sales began in February 2023.

taxes.value: 6% state tax on adult-use retail sales; local governments may add up to 3%, plus regular sales tax.

regulator.value: Division of Cannabis Regulation (DCR), part of the Department of Health and Senior Services.

dui.value: Impairment-based: Missouri has no THC per se or zero-tolerance law, so a cannabis DWI requires evidence of impairment.

tourists.value: Yes. Adults 21+ may buy up to 3 ounces per transaction. Visitors with an out-of-state medical card are protected from arrest for possessing up to Missouri's patient limits.

hemp_thc.value: Missouri's Intoxicating Cannabinoid Control Act (HB 2641) takes effect November 12, 2026: hemp-derived cannabinoid products, as the act defines them, are treated as marijuana under the Missouri Constitution, and their production and retail sale must be done only by businesses licensed by the Department of Health and Senior Services. Violations are a class D felony with a $5,000 fine per transaction; for some products the act applies only while federal hemp restrictions prohibit them, if Congress delays those restrictions.

timeline.event: Signature deadline passes; an initiative to regulate marijuana and hemp like alcohol does not make the 2026 ballot.
DCR publishes proposed rule amendments; public comment runs through December 2, 2026.

pending.item: Proposed amendments to DCR rules 19 CSR 100-1.070 and 1.100.
pending.status: Public comment open November 2 to December 2, 2026.

pending.item: SB 1187 would make public cannabis use a misdemeanor punishable by up to six months in jail.

faq.a: Yes. Adults 21 and older can buy and possess cannabis, and medical cannabis has been legal since 2018.

faq.q: How much weed can you have in Missouri?
faq.a: Adults may possess up to 3 ounces.

faq.q: Can you grow weed in Missouri?
faq.a: Yes, with a state cultivation registration, up to 6 flowering plants per registrant and 12 per home.

faq.q: What is the marijuana tax in Missouri?
faq.a: Adult-use purchases carry a 6% state tax, up to 3% in local tax, and regular sales tax.

sources.name: Missouri DHSS, Division of Cannabis Regulation
